New Yorkers woke up this Thanksgiving morning to drizzly, gray skies along with winds that had sidewalks covered in dead, yellow leaves, though the weather throughout the pre-noon hours was hardly the fearsome nor’easter blast that prompted the postponement till Saturday of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade.

Still, with wind levels of up to 23 mph - and gusts considerably stronger - the postponement appears to have been justified, and the worst of the storm is yet to come.

The impact of the postponement on performances that had been scheduled for today - marching bands, celebrity appearances, the big Broadway medley involving nine different shows - was still be dealt with as of this morning. While Coss didn't specify which performances are on schedule, Deadline can confirm that the Broadway medley that was planned in lieu of the traditional individual show performances is a go for Saturday. What Macy's is calling the " All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration " will go on as planned, with performers from The Lost Boys, The Rocky Horror Show, Wicked, Schmigadoon!, Aladdin, The Book of Mormon and Chicago confirmed. ( Hamiilton and the 30th-anniversary tribute to Rent have not weighed in yet, but sources say they are expected to participate).

Paddington the Musical is confirmed to participate in the Saturday broadcast as a separate float, as originally intended.

On Instagram today, Sherri Shepherd, currently portraying Genie in Broadway's Aladdin , wrote, "Winds won’t stop our participation in the Macys 100 Thanksgiving Day Parade, so tune in Saturday at 8:30am on NBC to catch myself and the cast of Aladdin perform!!" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

On the Schmigadoon! IG page, Brad Oscar, dressed and in character as the Mayor, said in a video, "As mayor of Schmigadoon, I have a proclamation: The Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed until Saturday at 8:30 a.m. on NBC. See you there."

The Book of Mormon had a simple message on its IG page about the date switch: "Ready and psyched."

As for other non-Broadway performers originally scheduled for Thursday, reports are filtering in piecemeal on whether they'll make the move to Saturday. The New York Post has reported that Smash Mouth will perform, and Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete are expected as well, as are the Radio City Rockettes. Other announcements should be coming in over the next day or two.

As for the marching bands, again, piecemeal reports. Texas' Pride of Pearland Marching Band reportedly raised an extra $350,000 in community donations to cover the additional housing and transportation costs to stay until Saturday, while other marching bands were either still scrambling or had made the decision to bow out of the event due to logistics. In the latter group are the Campo Verde High School Marching Band and some members of the Bowling Green State University Marching Band that were participating in a all-star band group.

Billy Evans , Elizabeth Holmes ’ partner and the father of their two children, took to X on Nov. 26 to write an emotional Thanksgiving message to her.

The text is primarily about how much he misses her and how their kids need their mother. Holmes is currently serving an 11-year prison sentence for four wire fraud-related convictions tied to her high-tech health company, Theranos.

“Today is our fourth Thanksgiving with Liz in prison,” Evans wrote. “Despite everything, I have so much to be thankful for. Our two beautiful kids, a love that’s only grown stronger through all of this. The incredible kindness of people who have stood beside us. I’m thankful for all the life we still have ahead of us. The memories yet to be made, the good we can still do in this world. articles.title: MCU Fantastic Four Reboot Lost Disney Money Despite $500 Million Box Office
articles.summary: If you don’t count Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Avengers: Doomsday, The Fantastic Four: First Steps was easily one of the most anticipated movies from Marvel Studios since Endgame. The film brought Marvel’s First Family into the MCU and laid the groundwork for Doomsday and seemed like it was off to an impressive start when […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you don’t count Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Avengers: Doomsday, The Fantastic Four: First Steps was easily one of the most anticipated movies from Marvel Studios since Endgame. The film brought Marvel’s First Family into the MCU and laid the groundwork for Doomsday and seemed like it was off to an impressive start when it hit theaters in July 2025. However, it turns out that the film may have made half a billion at the box office and still ended up losing money.

According to Forbes , The Fantastic Four: First Steps “exceeded the production budget” and ended up costing $371.1 million to make. When all of the accounting was said and done, including a $73.5 million reimbursement that reduced the film’s net spending to $297.6 million, once you account for the 50/50 split in box office earnings on the film’s $521.9 million earnings, the film came up $36.7 million short.

There’s actually a good bit about the revelation regarding The Fantastic Four: First Steps and its profitability that is interesting. The biggest might just be that this is a rare glimpse at the actual numbers behind the scenes. Generally speaking, we don’t get these specific disclosures — these sort of details aren’t the kind of things that get disclosed in the United States. However, the rules are a bit different in the U.K. Films made in the U.K. can benefit from specific credits and reimbursement based on percentage of production costs incurred in the U .K. which means the details have to be filed — and that’s where the numbers come from.

But beyond the very specific nerdiness of the money of it all, The Fantastic Four: First Steps is certainly not the only MCU film believed to have lost money. The Marvels , Thunderbolts* , Captain America: Brave New World , and The Incredible Hulk are all regularly cited as having lost money at the box office. It’s possible that Eternals is also among that list, though that’s somewhat disputed as the estimates are pretty tight. If you look at the movies that fall into the “poor box office” category here, however, there’s a bit of a pattern. These are movies that are more directly setting up themes, structure, and in some cases even characters that are necessary for future storytelling. I think that it’s worth considering that for many MCU fans, Marvel movies are largely defined by “big” characters they are already very familiar with. When you start bringing in other stories, those movies perform a little less well — but they’re just as important to the larger picture and the bigger story being told.

That in particular is something that we should see play out specifically when Avengers: Endgame hits theaters next month. After all, everything we’ve seen so far makes it pretty clear that the Fantastic Four play a significant part — and it’s already looking very good for that film’s box office.

Are you surprised about this detail about The Fantastic Four: First Steps’ box office? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: I Love The Emperor's New Groove, But David Spade Has Some Blunt Thoughts About Disney
articles.summary: You threw off my groove!
articles.content:
The Emperor’s New Groove is one of those Walt Disney Animation movies that will forever and always be imprinted in my brain. The 2000 film came out at just the right time in my childhood when I’d put it on repeat. I could honestly quote most of it front to back. However, I had no idea about the experience Kuzco's voice actor, David Spade , had.

Hey, he makes a good point. Prior to the 21st Century, animated movies weren't paying big-name celebrities the big bucks. David Spade was also working with Disney Animation at a time when the studio wasn’t making blockbusters to the degree it is now with the likes of Frozen or Moana . Spade even disclosed how much he made, saying this:

Shrek came out in 2001 – one year after The Emperor’s New Groove – and made almost half a billion worldwide. It helped usher in an era of blockbuster animated films led by A-list celebrities that we continue to live in. The Emperor's New Groove made $169 million worldwide, and was actually thought of as a commercial flop at the time of its release.

Animated movies like The Emperor’s New Groove famously go through a long production process. The 2000 movie in particular did so because it was actually originally an entirely different movie called Kingdom of the Sun . It was more inspired by The Prince and the Pauper , featured Owen Wilson in a voice role, and Spade was playing a character named Manco instead of Kuzco before they shifted directions. No wonder he was getting antsy while making it!

articles.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s “Encore” Extended Cut Will Include Cut Avengers: Doomsday Scene
articles.summary: New footage from the upcoming Spider-Man: (Brand New) Brand New Day re-release has been teased, confirming that a scrapped Avengers: Doomsday scene will appear. Ever since news broke that Sony Pictures' incredible summer blockbuster would return to theaters with extra scenes for audiences, the question of what they would be has had fans on edge. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google New footage from the upcoming Spider-Man: (Brand New) Brand New Day re-release has been teased, confirming that a scrapped Avengers: Doomsday scene will appear. Ever since news broke that Sony Pictures' incredible summer blockbuster would return to theaters with extra scenes for audiences , the question of what they would be has had fans on edge. We know for a fact that Rosario Dawson's return as Claire Temple will be restored for the film, and now it appears that Avengers: Doomsday footage will also be shown.

According to a report from The New York Times , spotlighting the upcoming box office potential of "Dunesday," the outlet reports that when Spider-Man: Brand New Day is re-released in theaters on December 4, it will include a "bonus" scene at the end of the film that is actually a scene already cut from Avengers: Doomsday . Though the content of the scene hasn't been confirmed, the outlet notes the footage is only meant to act as "an ad of sorts" for Avengers: Doomsday .

Even though Spider-Man: Brand New Day was pretty self-contained from the rest of the MCU in its narrative, Marvel fans still expected that the movie would at least have some kind of tease for Avengers: Doomsday since it was the last Marvel movie before its release. What happened, though, was a post-credit scene that only left fans confused , as Ned's spider-tracker began to "locate" Spider-Man and reveal he was no longer on Earth. Though clearly setting up something with the web-slinging hero, it elicited more of a "huh?" reaction than general enthusiasm.

Some Marvel fans interpreted the original post-credit scene in Spider-Man: Brand New Day as a tease of Tom Holland's character having a place in Battleworld for the upcoming Avengers: Secret Wars , while others thought it meant the arrival of one of the other Spider-Men from across the multiverse given the threat of an impending incursion. The trouble, of course, is that no one really knows what the scene means, which offers the Avengers: Doomsday footage that will be included in the re-release a chance to clear things up.

That said, the fact that the Doomsday footage that will appear in Spider-Man: (Brand New) Brand New Day is already noted as a deleted scene from the upcoming film may be just as frustrating for fans. Assuming that this footage in the film even hints at Tom Holland's Spider-Man, it could cause backlash, as fans assume his role was removed from the film itself. The good news is that Sony's encore re-release of Brand New Day will roll into theaters this time next week, with Doomsday set to follow just two weeks later.

Ahead of the re-release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day , though, the real reason behind its return to theaters is already clear. Despite Sony's movie already securing the record for the highest-grossing movie of all time at the domestic box office, the film is just a stone's throw away from being the first to make a billion dollars domestically. Assuming Marvel fans flock to the theater on the promise of new footage and a Doomsday tease, Sony might have just secured the movie's place in film history to an unbeatable degree.

Are you planning to go back to the theater to watch Spider-Man: (Brand New) Brand New Day ? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Want More Godzilla? Check Out Netflix's Anime Movie Trilogy
articles.summary: After the release of Godzilla Minus Zero, the smash-hit follow-up to 2023's Godzilla Minus One, fans of the kaiju franchise have been clamoring to find more content featuring their favorite reptilian titan. Thankfully, the Godzilla franchise has 72-years worth of content for fans to dive into, including Netflix's three part film series from Toho Animation […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After the release of Godzilla Minus Zero , the smash-hit follow-up to 2023's Godzilla Minus One , fans of the kaiju franchise have been clamoring to find more content featuring their favorite reptilian titan. Thankfully, the Godzilla franchise has 72-years worth of content for fans to dive into, including Netflix's three part film series from Toho Animation and Polygon Pictures. Consisting of Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters , Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle and Godzilla: The Planet Eater , this action-packed sci-fi trilogy tells a high-stakes story.

Initially introduced as a revenge journey that later pivots to focusing on the struggle between humans and nature, hubris, and the philosophy of what gives us an indomitable drive to survive, this unique Godzilla trilogy was penned by none other than Gen Urobuchi, a prolific and infamous writer known for his work on franchises like Puella Magi Madoka Magica , Psycho-Pass , and even legendary tokusatsu such as Kamen Rider Gaim . True to his other works, all three of these Godzilla films take their time unraveling their overarching narrative, using the legendary figure of Godzilla to aid in exploring the psychology of each of the main characters .

Opening with Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters in 2017 , the trilogy begins by introducing audiences to a group of human refugees returning to the planet Earth to attempt to recolonize it 20,000 years after being chased away by the titular kaiju. The film also introduces two alien species that worked in tandem when Earth was lost to the beast, known as the Exif, a group of religious zealots, as well as the technologically advanced Bilusaludo. After their failure to aid humanity in defeating Godzilla, humans emigrated to an exoplanet called "Tau-e."

The film's protagonist, Haruo Sakaki, holds a bitter hatred toward the kaiju and has made a vow to destroy it and reclaim Earth for humanity after deciding that Tau-e is inhabitable for human-kind's continued existence. The first film follows many story beats akin to a typical revenge story, but as the plot unravels it becomes clear that the first film is aiming to set up a "humans versus nature" conflict. Without giving too many details away, Planet of the Monsters leaves off on a cliffhanger that leads perfectly into its 2018 follow-up film, Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle .

Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle introduces another fan-favorite kaiju : Mechagodzilla who aids the returning human cast in their efforts to defeat Godzilla. The film is a direct sequel, opening shortly after the first entry's cliffhanger ending. The third and final film in the trilogy, The Planet Eater , leans heavily into themes of existential dread and human psychology, with the same extraterrestrial forces who once vowed to help humanity in their efforts now outwardly acting with hostility toward them due to differences in priorities when handling the threat of the giant kaiju threatening their recolonization efforts.

This film explores many classic story beats embedded into the roots of the Godzilla franchise as well, drawing comparisons between the beast and human-made tragedies. Directed in a collaborative effort by Kobun Shizuno ( Detective Conan, Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone ) and Hiroyuki Seshita ( Knights of Sidonia, Ajin ), the trilogy is uniquely positioned in how it presents these story beats, as it's the first Godzilla trilogy to commit fully to some of the franchise's sci-fi leanings and even giving Godzilla mutations akin to films like Shin Godzilla .

While the overall reception to the Netflix Godzilla trilogy is mixed in regards to how well the films stand as proper entries to the franchise, it's clear to see what the filmmaking team wanted to do with the story. In that, all three films beautifully accomplish exactly what they set out to do. Gen Urobuchi's scriptwriting prowess really hits its stride in the second film as the main cast's goals begin to unravel as they reckon with the consequences of pitting advanced technology against a hulking beast that's inhabited the Earth for well over 20,000 years.

Additionally, it's easy to see just how well the directing duo Kobun Shizuno and Hiroyuki Seshita understand psychological storytelling as it pertains to science fiction as a genre. The pair are able to showcase stunning sci-fi action sequences and large-scale kaiju fights that are interspersed with deeply compelling conversations about humanities position on the intergalactic food chain.All of this is only amplified by the absolutely phenomenal vocal performances found throughout the film trilogy, including Mamoru Miyano's role as the protagonist, Haruo Sakaki.

Mamoru Miyano has without a doubt positioned himself as an A-list casting choice for any anime series or film out there, with casting credits including legendary characters like Doma in Demon Slayer , Chrollo in Hunter x Hunter , and Light Yagami in Death Note . Other performances throughout the trilogy include other huge names in the industry, Takahiro Sakurai, Kana Hanazawa, Yuki Kaji, and Daisuke Ono.

For any Godzilla fan looking for a narratively compelling, bittersweet story of humanities conflict with nature, especially after the heartbreaking conclusion of Godzilla Minus Zero , there's truly no better option than binging Netflix's Godzilla trilogy. Have you checked out this trilogy yet? If so, what do you think of this take on Godzilla? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: The Screen-Matched Costume Used in One of the Scream Franchise's Most Shocking Moments is Hacking Out a Huge Price at Auction
articles.summary: Courtesy of Spyglass Media Group Horror movies are well known for falling in and out of favor with audiences over and over again throughout cinema history. In 1996, one film completely revived the slasher genre by leaning into its tropes and faults and turning them into a hugely successful franchise that is still going after three decades. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Horror movies are well known for falling in and out of favor with audiences over and over again throughout cinema history. In 1996, one film completely revived the slasher genre by leaning into its tropes and faults and turning them into a hugely successful franchise that is still going after three decades. The movie was Wes Craven's Scream , which delivered an opening sequence that completely caught audiences off guard and made an instantly iconic cinema moment. Now, the costume worn by Drew Barrymore in that iconic scene is up for auction with Prop Store , but if you want to own it, you will probably need to slash open your wallet and hope there is a lot of cash waiting to fall out.

What makes the horror genre successful has changed massively over the years, with fads and trends coming and going continually. Universal Monster movies and the like of the 30s died out by the end of the 1940s, slasher movies reignited the spark in the 1970s before becoming stale by the end of the 1980s. That meant the 1990s needed something new and although some dark psychological thrillers were keeping the genre ticking, it was down to old hand Wes Craven to really rejuvenate the horror genre for a new generation. After giving Freddy Krueger a new lease of life in 1994's Wes Craven's New Nightmare , the director turned his attention fully on the slasher genre he helped define a decade earlier and turned it on its head with the self-knowing Scream . A meta-film that subverted expectations of what a slasher movie was, Craven's biggest swing was to bring in Drew Barrymore as his poster girl and main trailer star only to have her brutally killed in the film's opening sequence.

While part of the fun on Scream was working out who was killing the residents of Woodsboro and why, the film's self-satire led to Craven pulling off one of the most audacious horror movie openings in history. After enlisting Drew Barrymore to be the poster girl and seemingly main "final girl" star of Scream , which the trailers certainly alluded to, Craven flipped the script by killing her character off in the first 15 minutes of the film. This was a bold move that only a master of the craft like Craven could come up with and it worked perfectly in line with the movie's meta take on the tropes that had been following the slasher genre like a knife-wielding stalker since the 1970s. The decision helped turn Scream into a massive hit and also helped bring Barrymore back into Hollywood on a more permanent basis.

Now, for Scream and Barrymore fans, the costume worn during the films brutal opening can be a new grail among someone's collection of movie memorabilia. The lot comes with the knitted sweater, bloodied trousers, blonde wig and even the rope and empty fake blood bottle from the production as part of an ensemble currently worth $40,000. Estimates expect this to rise, with a high-end of $80,000 being incredibly realistic for such an iconic piece of the Scream franchise's history. With the franchise currently in the middle of production on its eighth movie , there are plenty of long-term fans of the franchise that would be more than happy to give an original costume from the movie that started it all a home. For those looking for other Scream memorabilia, there are plenty of other items up for grabs including multiple Ghostface masks, Neve Campbell's trainers, jackets, named chair-backs and much more. The question isn't so much do you like scary movies, it is can you afford to buy a piece of one?

What do you think of the Scream franchise's most recent entries? Are they living up to Craven's original or should the whole thing be laid to rest? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 39 Years Ago, Marvel Predicted Avengers: Doomsday With A Wild Thanksgiving Parade Moment 80s Kids Will Never Forget
articles.summary: While the 2026 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade may have been postponed until this weekend, fans don't need to go without a dose of Marvel holiday spirit. To help set the stage for a nerdy holiday season, we're dusting off a 39-year-old clip from the 1987 parade, featuring the Marvel Universe float - which was packed […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While the 2026 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade may have been postponed until this weekend, fans don't need to go without a dose of Marvel holiday spirit. To help set the stage for a nerdy holiday season, we're dusting off a 39-year-old clip from the 1987 parade, featuring the Marvel Comics float - which was packed with now-iconic heroes, villains, and… RoboCop for a reason that I'll explain a bit further on.

The Marvel Comics parade float was sponsored by the publisher to promote its comic books, toys, and merchandise IP - long before the brand would venture into animated TV series and over two decades before the MCU would debut with Iron Man in 2008. Forty years later, the float is still a fun peice of 1980s nostalgia but, within the context of Doomsday set to arrive in mere weeks, it's also a fun preview of the two characters at the dead center of the Avengers mega-movie: Steve Rogers and Doctor Doom .

Check out a full clip of the float and its "story" below:

The clip includes a brief two minute "story" that sees Doctor Strange summon Captain America from the pages of a Marvel comic book to help Wolverine who is being attacked by Lady Loki and Magneto - only to confront Doctor Doom who has imprisoned Power Man (aka Luke Cage). Captain America, along with the help from RoboCop (we will get to that), frees Luke Cage and heads to take on more of the assembled bad guys - including Emma Frost and The Hulk (who is up to his "old tricks again"). The skit concludes with The Hulk toppling a clock tower before being incapacitated by Cap. Daredevil, Iron Man, Green Goblin, and more also appear. The entire thing is set to the iconic Back to the Future theme.

As for why RoboCop was on a Marvel Comics float in 1987, the original film that featured Alex Murphy's transformation into RoboCop had debuted in July of the same year - and went on to become a pop culture phenomenon; however, more importantly, Marvel Comics held a license to the character for comic books and other projects (Marvel actually produced the RoboCop animated series in 1988), so his appearance - while jarring from a first-party Marvel IP stand point, was actually a clever piece of cross-promotional branding that highlighted Marvel's reach in pop culture (even outside of their own characters).

The iconic Spider-Man balloon debuted the same year and, unlike the float, actually continued to make an appearance in the parade until bowing out in 1998. An updated Spider-Man balloon would return in 2009 and appear until returning in 2014 - a 5-year run that was not without controversy. In 2013, the Spider-Man balloon snagged on a tree - which ripped a large hole that caused the left arm to deflate.

Check out video of the 2013 Spider-Man balloon accident:

Fortunately, no one was hurt - except for maybe Spider-Man's pride. After returning 1 year later, the Spider-Man balloon took another length break - only returning for a single-year appearance in 2024 for the 85th anniversary of Marvel Comics.

There is no Marvel activation planned for the 2026 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

articles.title: Max Payne Remakes Get New Development Update From Remedy, But Still No Release Window
articles.summary: Courtesy of Remedy Entertainment With the releases of GTA 6 and Control Resonant, both Rockstar Games and Remedy Entertainment have more time to focus on the remakes of the Max Payne series, but despite good development updates, players still have no idea when these remakes will come out. Max Payne's first two titles have been known to be getting […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With the releases of GTA 6 and Control Resonant , both Rockstar Games and Remedy Entertainment have more time to focus on the remakes of the Max Payne series, but despite good development updates, players still have no idea when these remakes will come out. Max Payne 's first two titles have been known to be getting overhauls through restructured, modern versions ever since August 2024, when the projects were announced through a partnership between Rockstar and Remedy. While recent interviews reassure fans that the remakes are being made at a good rate, some players are concerned that no release window teases indicate that the games are further away than anyone imagined.

A large development update for the remade Max Payne games was given during an interview with Game File, specifically with Remedy Entertainment CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon. Gaudechon says that the status of the remake projects haven't really changed since 2024, reassuring players that everything is going along as planned. With the remake endeavor being listed as having the same budget as something like Alan Wake 2 at Remedy, there are certainly enough resources going into Max Payne 's revival, but fans are still worried due to the lack of any tangible information regarding the roadmap leading up to the remakes actually coming out.

Overall, the development update Remedy provided regarding the Max Payne 1 and Max Payne 2 remakes was positive, to a glaring degree. Following the extremely successful release of GTA 6 , Gaudechon had nothing but glowing things to say about Rockstar Games, saying they have "honestly been an awesome partner" throughout the process. Despite how players may feel about a lack of release window information, this is ultimately a good sign for the remakes' quality when more details are shown, as it indicates that development is leading to confidence at least on the side of Remedy.

According to Gaudechon again, this is due to the fact that "I think they're [Rockstar] super respectful of Remedy," with the feeling being mutual in the opposite direction. This mutual reverence for each other is likely enhanced even more by the success Remedy has had with Control Resonant , a game that sold one million copies in just three weeks. Both studios doing well for themselves has likely taken a lot of pressure off the scrutiny involved with the Max Payne remakes, especially if there is little friction like this praise suggests. At the very least, players have a clearer idea about how development is going through some genuinely good news.

That being said, players are understandably waiting for better clarity regarding details about the Max Payne remakes themselves, rather than just good tidings about developmental relationships. Rockstar's work on Max Payne 3 was divisive even though it was reviewed relatively well, so players are concerned that the gameplay of the remakes might match Rockstar's work more than Remedy's original vision. So, curiosity for the gameplay direction of the remakes are high, causing some players to ask why more hasn't been shared two years following the project's confirmation.

Another three to four updates of Remedy praising Rockstar or Rockstar praising Remedy would be great, but eventually, players are going to want to see something. The Max Payne remakes are eagerly anticipated projects bringing back highly underrated shooters, which helped establish tropes seen in others title since. The slow motion gunplay of Max Payne would inspire Rockstar series like Red Dead Redemption and GTA 6 in many ways, so their involvement is great in these remakes. At this time of writing, though, players have no idea how the gameplay of the remakes will reflect Rockstar's or Remedy's design philosophies.

Given the budget comparisons to Alan Wake 2 , there is certainly going to be a lot of gameplay for Max Payne 's remakes. Yet, now that Control Resonant and GTA 6 have come out, players are going to start wondering where the Max Payne games are, since both studios now have more time to devote to those projects. Should no gameplay nor release date be revealed before the halfway point of 2027, fans could grow even more nervous with suspicions of delays or cancellations. In the shaky state of the gaming industry, you never know.

The best thing Remedy and Rockstar can do is provide some sort of trailer at an upcoming game-related event, such as the 2026 Game Awards if they have enough gameplay to show. A release window would also be huge at this type of event, but the busy work on GTA 6 and Control Resonant could mean any substantial news for the remakes are still a long ways off. At the very least, fans can be happy that the relationship between Remedy and Rockstar is a strong one, at least ensuring that the Max Payne remakes won't be forgot about anytime soon.

articles.title: New Digimon Game Available for Free
articles.summary: A new Digimon game is available, and it is free. Right now, the new release is smartphone-only, and there is no word of it coming to Nintendo, PC, PlayStation, or Xbox platforms. This could change in the future, but currently, if you want to play the new Digimon game, you will need to download it […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new Digimon game is available, and it is free. Right now, the new release is smartphone-only, and there is no word of it coming to Nintendo, PC, PlayStation, or Xbox platforms. This could change in the future, but currently, if you want to play the new Digimon game, you will need to download it from the App Store or via Google Play. It is available in 183 countries, and it is 100% free as a free-to-play game. To this end, the initial download is free and you don't have to spend a dime on it to play it, and enjoy it, but spending is encouraged by the game's design and structure.

The new Digimon game from Bandai Namco is Digimon Alysion , which is a new digital card game and effectively the digital version of the Digimon Trading Card Game , complete with its own story, characters, cards, and online battles. It's a classic digital card game with Digimon. To this end, it's for both die-hard hardcore fans of the long-running series and more casual ones who may have grown up with the franchise, but haven't been active with it in a while. Particularly, with how expensive the physical card game is to get into, this digitized version is a great entry point before committing to the costs that come wth playing physically. And the game iss pretty good, or at least that is what user reviews for it so far suggest. To this end, it has a 4.5 out of 5 stars on the App Store. Meanwhile, it has 3.5 out of 5 stars on Google Play, which isn't as good, but is still a decent rating.

Most user reviews note the game is reminiscent of Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel quite a bit, which is a reasonable comparison. And like most card games at launch, it has a good foundation, but could be fleshed out with more content and more quality-of-life features, both of which it will no doubt get in the future. Meanwhile, negative reviews highlight the game's long tutorial, its voice acting, and some feel the game is overly complicated. In particular, the English voice acting takes a beating, and is even cited as being poor in many positive 5/5 star reviews.

Digimon Fans Are Enjoying the New Release It's worth noting that while there are an appreciable number of negative reviews, the majority of reviews are very positive and perfect 5/5 scores. Some are certainly bouncing off the game, but so far it appears Bandai Namco has done a solid job in replicating the TCG in digital form.

"One of the best card games out right now. The app more or less simulates the real game perfectly, fun to play, awesome art, even some cool 3D cutscenes," reads one 5/5 user review on Googe Play.

What the future of the game is, and how frequent its updates will be, remains to be seen. Bandai Namco did announce, though, that because the game passed 450,000 pre-registrations, all players will receieve tickets to redeem for game-exclusive cards, card packs, and one secret rare card, with more rewards coming in the future.

The chatter got so loud that Grande took a step away from the public , although she recently reunited with Bowen Yang and talked about the backlash to her "Petal" music video.

Clearly the 33 year-old singer saw the comments online, and backlash related to a change in her sound, the years-long Wicked promotional tour, as well as her personal appearance. Ariana Grande set some boundaries to care for her mental health, but she also seemingly stands by her artistic choices related to the "Petal" music video. articles.title: 7 Different Origin Stories for How the Joker Became the Clown Prince of Crime
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics The Joker is the most iconic and terrifying supervillain in comic book history. For decades, the Clown Prince of Crime has terrorized Gotham and DC Comics. But despite his infamy, no one’s exactly sure who he is, including it seems the Joker himself. The Joker likes to say that he prefers his origin story to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Joker is the most iconic and terrifying supervillain in comic book history. For decades, the Clown Prince of Crime has terrorized Gotham and DC Comics . But despite his infamy, no one’s exactly sure who he is, including it seems the Joker himself. The Joker likes to say that he prefers his origin story to be a multiple choice, which has led to many possible explanations for his existence. No backstory has been proven true, and the Joker keeps making up new ones to keep things interesting. While we may never know the truth, these possible origins have shaped our understandings of the Joker.

With a character like the Joker, his origins can range from the tragic to the terrifying. Almost everyone tries, in some form, to explain how a monster like the Joker could have been created and how he started his eternal rivalry with Batman .

When Batman sat on the Mobius Chair and gained omnipotence during the “Darkseid War,” his first question was the Joker’s real identity. However, the Mobius Chair answered, “There are three.” And with that, DC Comics introduced the highly contentious retcon that there’s not one, but three Jokers. The controversial Three Jokers story explores this revelation, where Gotham is plagued by a trio of Jokers, each representing a different era of the character. These Jokers are the calculating Criminal of the Golden Age, the wacky Clown of the Silver Age who killed Jason Todd, and the psychopathic Comedian of the Bronze and Modern Ages who paralyzed Barbara Gordon. Naturally, it’s also suggested that two of these Jokers were created by the original, whichever one that may be. To this day, people argue over the canonicity of this story and which one of them, if any, is the true Joker. But then again, it’s very in-character for the Joker to make his own origin even more confusing.

Most possible Joker origins involve him getting soaked in toxic chemicals as an adult, which caused him to go insane. Yet Batman Vol. 2 #23.1 in 2013 gave the Joker a childhood so traumatic that it would have been impossible for him not to lose his mind. In this retelling, the Joker explains that, when he was a young boy, he lived with his abusive and murderous Aunt Eunice. The young boy was beaten, starved, and isolated every single day. But the worst revelation was that Aunt Eunice would regularly brush her nephew down with bleach. Naturally, this treatment would eventually lead to the Joker’s skin turning pure white. Aunt Eunice would also constantly gloat about how she brutally tortured and murdered her late husband to make her nephew even more terrified of her. Unlike other Joker origins that involve one terrible accident, his backstory in this issue shows how he was molded by the twisted woman who raised, abused, and disfigured him for years.

For all the death and destruction that the Joker causes, most people recognize that, at the end of the day, he’s still human. That was until the events of “Endgame,” which suggested the Clown Prince of Crime was something far older and more malevolent. The storyline proposes that for centuries, Gotham City has been plagued by a monster called the Pale Man who has claimed countless lives. The leading theory behind the Pale Man’s existence is that he was a man who came into contact with dionesium, an ingredient from Ra’s al Ghul’s Lazarus Pit. This substance made the person immortal, and he spent the next several centuries terrorizing the people of Gotham like a Boogeyman. What “Endgame” suggested was that the Joker is the Pale Man, and therefore an inhuman monster that can’t be killed. The Joker advocated this origin more than anyone. Although Batman eventually disproved this theory, it most likely played a part in inspiring the Absolute Joker.

One of the Joker’s most defining characteristics is his obsession with Batman. However, “Lovers and Madmen” turns this obsession into the catalyst that created the Clown Prince of Crime. In this retelling, the Joker is a ruthless bank robber named Jack who’s committed dozens of robberies. But after succeeding so many times, Jack grows bored with the profession. That was until a young Batman arrives and foils Jack’s latest scheme. Feeling he’d met a true rival and found a new purpose, Jack began committing bigger and deadlier robberies to get Batman’s attention. When Batman and Jack battle again, the Dark Knight throws a batarang that accidentally slices Jack’s mouth, giving him his iconic, gruesome grin. Batman gets so desperate to stop Jack’s rampage that he enlists the help of mobsters to track Jack down. When the mobsters try to execute Jack at a chemical factory, he escapes by falling into a vat that bleaches his skin white and turns his hair green. Since then, the Joker’s obsession with Batman hasn’t wavered.

When the Joker was first introduced, he was a complete enigma with no real name or backstory. DC Comics gave its very first possible origin for the Joker in Detective Comics #168 . There, the Joker explains that he was once a normal lab worker who decided to steal a million dollars from his employer, the Monarch Playing Card Company. To pull off the heist, the Joker created the Red Hood persona and costume. After stealing the money, the Joker swam through a sewer of chemical waste to avoid detection. The Red Hood helmet provided the Joker with an oxygen supply, so he didn’t drown. Unfortunately, when he emerged from the chemical waste and took off the helmet, the Joker discovered the chemicals had turned his body chalk white and his hair green. This revelation drove him mad and led him to become the Clown Prince of Crime. Most Joker origin stories use his former identity as the Red Hood and his dip in chemicals, so this revelation was highly influential.

When you dress up like a clown and kill innocent people for fun, chances are that you’re insane. Indeed, no matter how atrocious his actions are, the worst that ever happens to the Joker is that he’s thrown into Arkham Asylum because he’s considered to be legally insane. However, “Case Study” suggests it’s all a lie and that the Joker is a rational, natural-born monster. In notes written by Dr. Harleen Quinzel before her turn to villainy, she hypothesizes that the Joker was once a clever, elusive crime boss who killed for pleasure and to expand his territory. After carving his way through the criminal underworld, he created the Red Hood identity for the thrill. This led to his heist at a chemical plant, where, after Batman confronted him, he accidentally fell into a vat of acid. But where other versions of the Joker went mad from the deformity, this one only pretended to go insane. Now free from the threat of capital punishment, the Joker knows that nothing can stop his sadism.

No Joker story is more iconic than Alan Moore’s masterful yet controversial graphic novel The Killing Joke . This story not only reworked earlier ideas about the Joker’s origins but also added a new level of tragedy that led the Clown Prince of Crime to develop his terrifying philosophy. In this version, the Joker was once a kind but struggling comedian who desperately tried to make ends meet to support his pregnant wife. He was eventually approached by the mob, who offered him a lot of money to pretend to be the Red Hood while they robbed a chemical plant. But on the day of the robbery, the comedian learned that his wife died in a fire. This tragedy didn’t stop the mobsters from forcing the comedian to go through with the heist anyway. During the robbery, they were confronted by Batman, who assumed that the comedian was the ringleader. Their confrontation ended with he comedian falling into the vat of acid. This tragedy not only created the Joker but also led to his philosophy that all it takes is one bad day for someone to turn out just like him.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google New Avengers: Doomsday footage just showed that Ian McKellen's Magneto is no match for Robert Downey Jr.'s Doom. The trailers and footage from the upcoming Marvel movie have already gone heavy on the threat that the beloved comic book villain poses in the new movie, which means it hasn't shied away from showing him defeating beloved heroes. From the start, Doom making mincemeat of Thor has been one of the most prominent scenes in the marketing, but now we see him defying the powers of one of the X-Men's most powerful.

In a new TV spot released by Marvel, the Avengers: Doomsday footage shows Magneto attempting to overpower Doom by removing his metal mask. This is something that fans have been wondering about ever since McKellen's return as the omega-level mutant was confirmed, since it appeared to be a slam dunk in terms of having a character that could easily defeat him . As you can see from the footage, though, the will of Doom appears stronger than Magneto's power, as his mask removal is quickly squashed by magic.

He is extinction. Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18. Get tickets now: https://t.co/HReh5UfF1M pic.twitter.com/FmZjxLSiew

As Marvel fans know well, Magneto is often associated with the most powerful mutants across the history of the comics . Though the version McKellen is playing on screen in the film is clearly one that's gotten up there in years, that hasn't changed the potency of his abilities. Not only does the footage confirm this in how he's able to begin the process of ripping Doom's mask off, but in how it can resist Doom's magic at least for a time.

That said, McKellen's Magneto has pretty pointed dialogue about Doom, adding: "He is pain. He is extinction." It's worth noting that Magneto's right arm is the one he's using to try and rip Doom's mask off in the footage, with another scene showing the same arm in a sling. So not only does it appear that Doom can resist Magneto's powers with his magic, but he gives him a major physical injury, something that he's never really experienced on the big screen.

Though this new Avengers: Doomsday is showing just how threatening Robert Downey Jr.'s character will be in the film, it's being met with a mixed response, not because fans find it unbelievable or bad, but because they don't want anything else ruined ahead of the film's release.

"Marvel it’s enough. You can rest now. We are all going to see the movie. It will make 3B relax," wrote a user in response to the TV spot. Another added, "Alright yall showing a little toooooo much now." Finally, in keeping with tradition, one fan said: "At this rate we will have watched the film before its released."

With three weeks left until release, Marvel fans should start to brace for the potential of this becoming more common. Despite the level of secrecy that Marvel Studios often puts on its films during development, production, and pre-release, the time just before that theatrical debut is when footage that may be considered spoilery is revealed to the world.

What do you make of the new Avengers: Doomsday footage? Do you think Magneto is actually defeated by Doom or is it a trick or editing? Give us your take in the comments below.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Director Says MCU Crossover Is More Ambitious Than Endgame for 1 Reason
articles.summary: Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday will see different realities of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (aka different eras of Marvel movie franchises) all going to war to see who gets to march proudly into the future franchise – and which characters (and actors) we'll say goodbye to for the final time. The roster of characters is huge: the MCU […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday will see different realities of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (aka different eras of Marvel movie franchises) all going to war to see who gets to march proudly into the future franchise – and which characters (and actors) we'll say goodbye to for the final time. The roster of characters is huge: the MCU will be defended by Sam Wilson's (Anthony Mackie) Avengers team (Falcon, Shang-Chi, Thor), Yelena Belova's (Florence Pugh) "New Avengers" squad, the combined might of Wakanda and Namor's Talokan nation, with the Fantastic Four (and some key allies they recruit) lending a hand from Earth-828. On the other side, the X-Men of the Fox movie universe (Earth-10005) will be fighting with mutant might to keep their world alive, while cosmic players like Loki, the Time Variance Authority will be trying to keep the entire multiverse alive.

Just describing all of that, it should surprise no one that Avengers: Doomsday co-director Joe Russo is boasting that this is the most ambitious crossover event that the MCU (or any major franchise) has ever done.

During EW's coverage of Avengers: Doomsday , Joe Russo didn't hold back about the scale of what he and brother Anthony Russo have built with Doomsday . "By far and away the most ambitious project we’ve ever attempted is the convergence of 25 years of storytelling, all the way back to the first X-Men in 2000," Russo said. "It’s three major franchises crashing into each other. So the real work was around trying to give each group a collective arc that the audience could follow and root for them."

Reed Richards actor Pedro Pascal echoed that same sentiment, stating, "It’s the biggest ensemble I’ve ever been a part of. To put us all in a room together, you would expect it to feel atomic. And yet it was like [an] immediate family. It was really warm. No one was alone; that was for sure.”

The meta-layers of Avengers: Doomsday are already apparent, as the film will be a bittersweet send-off for any number of Marvel movie franchises older fans grew up with, or enjoyed as pioneering adaptations of Marvel characters, before the MCU took the reins. Now, Doomsday and its sequel , Avengers: Secret Wars , will clear the board and reset the franchise, offering viewers a complete collection of Marvel characters all in one place, for the very first time. But that consolidated franchise will come at the cost of ending the arcs of beloved characters of yesteryear, and (more painfully), saying goodbye to some iconic performances, or (tragically, in the case of Patrick Stewart) some iconic performers.

The (confirmed) cast of Avengers: Doomsday includes Robert Downey Jr. as Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom, Chris Evans as Steve Rogers, Chris Hemsworth as Thor, Pedro Pascal as Reed Richards/Mister Fantastic, Paul Rudd as Scott Lang/Ant-Man, Anthony Mackie as Sam Wilson/Captain America, Florence Pugh as Yelena Belova/Black Widow, Vanessa Kirby as Sue Storm/Invisible Woman, Ebon Moss-Bachrach as Ben Grimm/Thing, Wyatt Russell as John Walker/U.S. Agent, Channing Tatum as Remy LeBeau/Gambit, Simu Liu as Shang-Chi, Hayley Atwell as Peggy Carter, Tom Hiddleston as God Loki, James Marsden as Scott Summers/Cyclops, Joseph Quinn as Johnny Storm/Human Torch, Sebastian Stan as Bucky Barnes/Winter Soldier.

Also appearing are David Harbour as Alexei Shostakov/Red Guardian, Letitia Wright as Shuri/Black Panther, Lewis Pullman as Bob Reynolds/Sentry, Kelsey Grammer as Hank McCoy/Beast, Kathryn Newton as Cassie Lang, Danny Ramirez as Joaquín Torres/Falcon, Winston Duke as M'Baku, Alan Cumming as Kurt Wagner/Nightcrawler, Hannah John-Kamen as Ava Starr/Ghost, Rebecca Romijn as Raven Darkhölme/Mystique, Hailee Steinfeld as Kate Bishop/Hawkeye, Tenoch Huerta as Namor, Mabel Cadena as Namora, Alex Livinalli as Attuma, with Ian McKellen as Erik Lehnsherr/Magneto, and Patrick Stewart as Charles Xavier/Professor X.

Leading up to Doomsday 's release, other MCU projects have revealed that Mark Ruffalo's Bruce Banner/Hulk and Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff/Scarlet Witch are both part of the film, while Hugh Jackman's Logan/Wolverine and Ryan Reynolds' Wade WIlson/Deadpol have both been teased. Loki cast members Tara Strong (Miss Minutes), Owen Wilson (Mobius M. Mobius), Ke Huy Quan (Ouroboros, "O.B.") will also be making an appearance.

Avengers: Doomsday will be released in theaters on December 18th.

Mark Tildesley , one of the industry's most respected production designers, has passed away aged 63.

Tildesley's many credits include James Bond movie No Time To Die , 28 Days Later , The Constant Gardener , The Two Popes , Jay Kelly , Joseph Kosinski’s F1: The Movie , and Sam Mendes' upcoming Beatles movies. Mendes today described his collaborator as "entirely original and extraordinarily gifted".

Boyle and Tildesley memorably teamed up for the 2012 London Olympics opening ceremony, a feat that earned the production designer an Emmy win alongside Suttirat Anne Larlarb.

With Mendes he made Empire Of Light and was aboard for the upcoming T he Beatles — A Four-Film Cinematic Event alongside Stefania Cella and Neal Callow.

He won three British Film Designers Guild awards, for High-Rise, Empire of Light and F1: The Movie , as well as a Set Decorators Society of America prize, an Art Directors Guild award, and a British Independent Film Award.

Mendes said today: "Mark was a one-off: gentle, funny, warm, mischievous, entirely original and extraordinarily gifted. My abiding memory of him is from Empire of Light , flying down the Margate seafront on a motorised scooter, his technicolored scarf flapping in the wind, twinkling like a schoolboy playing hooky. Besides being a well-respected and extremely talented production designer he was a friend and colleague to many of our members and will be very much missed by everyone in the Industry who knew and worked with him.”

articles.title: Marvel Took a Huge Gamble With Secret Wars, and It Created the Modern Comic Book Event
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics In 1984, Marvel Comics released one of the most important comic book crossover series ever made. Before this, the closest that Marvel came to a giant event series was either stories mostly focused on one book, like "The Kree-Skrull War" in the 1970s, or Marvel Super Heroes Contest of Champions, with heroes forced to fight […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In 1984, Marvel Comics released one of the most important comic book crossover series ever made. Before this, the closest that Marvel came to a giant event series was either stories mostly focused on one book, like "The Kree-Skrull War" in the 1970s, or Marvel Super Heroes Contest of Champions , with heroes forced to fight each other for the Grandmaster and Death in a contest with the Collector's life in the balance. However, Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars was unlike anything Marvel or DC had ever attempted in the past. This was the first major site-wide crossover series, and it changed everything about how comic books were made from that point on.

Even before Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars #1 (1984) by Jim Shooter and Michael Zeck came out, Marvel was already shaking up the entire brand in the most innovative way possible.

I was a kid when Marvel Comics prepared to start its Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars comic book series, and I had no idea what was going on. For most of my reading life, I was following mostly single and small multi-issue stories, and even when comic books crossed over, it was a big deal. DC Comics had the Justice League and Justice Society team up annually, and that was a huge event because these things had never happened before. When Marvel Super Heroes Contest of Champions came out in 1982, it was incredible, especially for a kid who had never dreamed he would see so many heroes fighting in one series.

What Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars did was take that idea and blow up the entire Marvel Universe. That is because Marvel showed before the series was even underway that it was going to change everything in Marvel and reset several major titles. This all started on the last page of most major comics published in January 1984, where the heroes went to Central Park and ended up disappearing without a trace. These moments in comics featuring Spider-Man, the X-Men, the Hulk, the Avengers, Captain America, Iron Man, and the Fantastic Four left it a mystery as to what happened.

What makes this so amazing is that the results of Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars were shown before the miniseries even hit its second issue. That is because all the heroes were back the next month, and there were major changes that happened without any explanation. First up, Spider-Man returned with a new black costume in The Amazing Spider-Man #252 , and Spider-Man could put it on and take it off by just commanding it with his mind. It took seven months before Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars #8 came out and showed him getting the costume, and it took even longer to prove this was a symbiote.

The Fantastic Four was back, but The Thing was no longer with them. In fact, the solo The Thing series had him on a barren planet having adventures while the Fantastic Four introduced the world to their newest team member, She-Hulk. It wasn't until Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars ended that The Thing's departure was explained. Colossus and Kitty Pryde's relationship was destroyed when he told Kitty about his relationship with Zsaji on Battleworld, which was a good thing thanks to their age difference. The miniseries took a while to show what Colossus did and who Zsaji even was.

Magneto came back with a new attitude, and Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars showed why he started his change from a villain to an antihero and eventually an actual X-Men member. The Hulk returned with an injured leg, and his intelligence was lessened a great deal, returning him more in line with his Savage Hulk persona. It was a huge reset for Magneto and the Hulk, and once again, it took several months to show what caused the changes in both men. Nothing like this had ever happened before in comics, and it changed everything in Marvel and DC.

In Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars , a cosmic entity known as the Beyonder captured heroes and villains from Earth and forced them to fight each other. This was all based on the Beyonder's curiosity to understand humans. He offered the winning side anything they wished for, which was very enticing for the villains. The heroes mostly wanted to just get back home. What happened next was a story of betrayals, intense battles, and awe-inspiring moments. The X-Men split off from the other heroes, refusing to trust anyone, while villains like Doctor Doom attempted to capture all the Beyonder's power for himself.

Spider-Man had his costume destroyed and found a machine that created a new one that he thought he controlled using his brainwaves. The Hulk had one of the most powerful moments in his history when he held up an entire mountain to save all the heroes. Spider-Man fought the X-Men and held his own to prove his power. By the end, everyone was back home except for The Thing, and nothing was the same.

This led to several similar series. Marvel released a sequel to Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars , although it had the Beyonder coming to Earth and disrupting life on the planet. Even more importantly, one year later, DC Comics released Crisis on Infinite Earths , which had a similar format where all the Earth's heroes had to stand up and unite to fight a being called the Anti-Monitor. In just two years, Marvel and DC each had a series that threw everyone into one comic book storyline and then shook up the entire universe when it was done.

In today's comic book world, there are often multiple site-wide crossover events every year. In 2026 alone, there have been "Avengers: Armageddon," "Queen in Black," and the upcoming "DNX." Titles like "Civil War," "Annihilation," "Secret Empire," and "House of M" wouldn't have existed without Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars . The 2015 "Secret Wars" event only exists because of this earlier series . Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars not only blew the mind of a kid who loved comics, but also changed how the major companies published their series.

articles.title: GTA 6 Could Shape Rockstar Games’ Most Exciting Sequel, But Not in the Way You Think
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has continually pushed the boundaries of what open-world video games can accomplish, and Grand Theft Auto 6 is the pinnacle of its accomplishments. While most players are excited to explore Vice City and partake in the numerous activities, the technology behind the game cannot be overlooked. The attention to detail surpasses even Red […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Rockstar Games has continually pushed the boundaries of what open-world video games can accomplish, and Grand Theft Auto 6 is the pinnacle of its accomplishments. While most players are excited to explore Vice City and partake in the numerous activities, the technology behind the game cannot be overlooked. The attention to detail surpasses even Red Dead Redemption 2, which broke ground when it launched. The studio excels at creating believable environments and NPCs, which has implications that extend well beyond the Grand Theft Auto series.

Naturally, many fans are looking forward to Red Dead Redemption 3 , myself included. But there is another overlooked game that deserves a sequel, and GTA 6 proves a sequel to L.A. Noire could be Rockstar's greatest yet. The 2011 detective game is one of the best in its genre , with its emphasis on investigating crime scenes, interrogating suspects, and interpreting human behavior. As impressive as those systems were at the time, they could reach an entirely new level with the modern tech that created GTA 6 .

One of the biggest selling points of L.A. Noire was its MotionScan technology, which captured actors’ facial performances and translated them into the game. Players had to study facial expressions, listen to testimony, and examine evidence to determine whether someone was lying. This was incredibly ambitious for a 2011 game, and it has mixed success. With how far facial animations have come since then, particularly in GTA 6 , Rockstar could make interrogations considerably better.

I'd love to see the attention and detail of GTA 6's NPCs be applied to L.A. Noire 2 . A nervous witness might appear suspicious despite telling the truth, while an experienced criminal could maintain their composure throughout an interrogation. Players could study changes in posture, vocal delivery, and interactions with other characters rather than simply waiting for someone to avoid eye contact. Physical evidence would consequently become even more important when establishing whether someone was being dishonest.

Rockstar could also expand interrogations to have different effects and outcomes based on location. Questioning someone at their workplace might produce different results than confronting them at the police station. Establishing trust with a witness could encourage them to reveal information they previously withheld. The realistic character performances and NPC interactions of Grand Theft Auto 6 could make L.A. Noire 2 Rockstar's most focused game yet.

For all its accomplishments, the original L.A. Noire never took full advantage of its open world. Its recreation of 1947 Los Angeles was impressive, but much of the city existed as scenery between investigations. Players could respond to street crimes and discover collectibles, but they provided little support to the overall package. A sequel built using the technology behind GTA 6 could finally address this shortcoming by making the city itself part of the investigative process.

I would love to investigate a murder without being explicitly told where to go next. Players could canvass neighborhoods, question shopkeepers, follow suspects, and observe their daily routines. Rockstar could supply the obvious hints through NPCs, but layer more detailed clues and mysteries with more obscure interactions that only come through exploring beyond the obvious route. Time-sensitive evidence or NPCs who react based on your reputation or actions could bring new levels to the investigator genre.

Even the smaller environmental details could become relevant to investigations. Footprints, damaged vegetation, discarded cigarettes, and misplaced objects could provide clues that players might otherwise overlook. Rather than relying on musical cues or controller vibrations to identify evidence, players could learn to search for and recognize inconsistencies within their surroundings. Rockstar's worlds have incredible details, and L.A. Noire 2 could fully utilize this in its gameplay like no other game from the studio.

As much as I loved Red Dead Redemption 2 , I would rather Rockstar revisit the detective genre than take us back to the Wild West. Arthur Morgan’s adventure already explored the decline of the American frontier, and it remains a masterpiece. It's hard to imagine Rockstar topping it, while L.A. Noire has so much potential, both mechanically and narratively, that modern hardware could finally do justice. It is the dark horse pick, but one I think would be particularly successful today.

There is also no reason a sequel would need to return to 1940s Los Angeles. Rockstar could explore organized crime in 1950s Chicago, corruption in 1970s New York, or even the criminal underworld of 1980s Miami. Each setting would offer different investigative challenges, historical events, criminal organizations, and storytelling opportunities. Rockstar's experience recreating different periods of American history makes the possibilities nearly endless.

Of course, Rockstar has not officially announced L.A. Noire 2 , and there is no confirmation that it is in development. Not only that, but Rockstar is probably focused on getting GTA Online up-and-running for GTA 6 rather than developing a new game. But god do I want L.A. Noire 2 , so much so that I'd sacrifice Red Dead Redemption 3 and Grand Theft Auto 7 . Instead of building another open world centered on committing crimes, in the Wild West or modern day, Rockstar could surprise everyone by creating its most ambitious game about solving them.

articles.title: Following Dermot Mulroney’s Exit From Chicago Fire, I Needed To Know If Pascal Could Come Back
articles.summary: Pascal needs to come back to 51.
articles.content:
Chicago Fire is now in its 15 th season on the 2026 TV schedule , and this season the show has gone through some casting changes. Original cast member Joe Miñoso officially exited as Joe Cruz in the 300 th episode, but he wasn’t the only one to do so. After just a couple of seasons, Dermot Mulroney said goodbye to Firehouse 51, departing as Battalion Chief Dom Pascal in the Season 15 premiere. He was solid in the role, however, and I wanted to know if he’d ever come back.

Even though we just said goodbye to him, new showrunner Victor Teran told CinemaBlend about the possibility of Pascal popping up at 51 again. He told me "anything's possible" and elaborated on that, telling CinemaBlend the connection with Severide could indicate more down the line.

Unlike a lot of characters on TV who get killed off, Chicago Fire included, Pascal's story was left open. He left 51 in Kelly’s hands and, as Teran pointed out, is now building his career in Arizona. That said, he became close with the firehouse and obviously made a mark in a short amount of time, and made sure that Kelly was ready to take over. I would love nothing more than to see Pascal again, and I could not be happier to hear Teran's response. Since Mulroney was not happy about the exit , he probably wouldn't be opposed to coming back.

articles.title: Nathan Fillion's Firefly Update Is Good News for the Revival, Even If It's Not What I Expected

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Firefly revival, which will be an animated series, is still progressing despite no news over the past eight months. Earlier this year, after more than twenty years of waiting by very loyal Brown Coats, Firefly 's return to television was confirmed when Nathan Fillion himself revealed that an animated series that would revive the show as officially in the works. Anticipation has only built in the time since then, even though Fillion's last update didn't inspire confidence .

Now, the Firefly star has given a more optimistic take on the show's progress. Speaking with Patton Oswalt on the Revenge Of podcast, the star confirmed it's still happening, with a surprising tease. "Listen, things happened, but albeit very slowly. But things are still moving forward," Fillion said. "Not in the way I thought it would, but in more ways, yes, I'm getting more yeses than I am nos, which is wonderful."

Fillion's tease about getting "more yeses than nos" bodes well for the potential of Firefly 's revival actually happening , and feels like the opposite of what you might expect for a sequel show happening decades later. The good news for the series is that its cult status in the 2000s, which was enough to get it a feature film continuation after the show was cancelled, is actually a commodity that has become a hot ticket in Hollywood. Shows that were once seen as a failure and something studios wanted to avoid have now become the kind of property that the modern streaming environment is eager to revive.

The good news for the Firefly revival, which will no doubt help in its quest to find a distributor, is that most of the original cast is set to return; in addition to Fillion, original stars Alan Tudyk, Gina Torres, Jewel Staite, Morena Baccarin, Sean Maher, Summer Glau, and Adam Baldwin are all expected to reprise their roles. Only 1 role is expected to be recast when the show is put together, with Fillion previously confirming that Shepherd Book would appear with a new voice actor playing the part; original star Ron Glass passed away in 2016 at the age of 71.

20th Television Animation has teamed with Fillion’s production banner, Collision33, for the Firefly revival, which has been given its blessing by original creator Joss Whedon, who is not involved. Instead, the new series has tapped Marc Guggenheim ( Arrow ) and Tara Butters ( Agent Carter ) to serve as showrunners.

Major questions remain about the actual content of the Firefly revival, though, namely, when will it take place in the larger continuity of the series? Though we got fourteen episodes of the original series, the Serenity sequel movie ended with the crew's actions causing major changes to the larger lore , and that's on top of big character deaths.

Given that Alan Tudyk is set to return, we can assume that the animated show will be set before the events of Serenity , but that then presents a problem in how the show handles Summer Glau's River Tam. The film not only offered real answers for the character's history, but also gave her a new role on the crew. With more than twenty years of time to think about what this show might look like, though, we anticipate they'll have an answer for it all in the end.

articles.title: John Mulaney Had To Cut A Segment From His Stand-Up Special After Fast Food Joke Went VERY Wrong
articles.summary: A simple question about a fast-food restaurant can completely derail a comedian's plans.
articles.content:
With plenty of comedy on the 2026 Netflix streaming schedule , I've always appreciated how John Mulaney can take something ordinary and turn it into an absurdly funny story. Whether he's talking about taking his Korean in-laws to CVS, his children saying scary things, or any number of his hilarious stand-up jokes , his delivery makes even the most ridiculous observations sound perfectly reasonable. Although apparently, one fast-food joke didn't survive the trip from the comedy club to one of his specials, and the reason is pretty hilarious.

According to Smith, the response left Mulaney unsure how to continue, so he simply moved on to his next bit. I have to assume that's not how the comedian was expecting things to god own.

When the finished special eventually premiered, Smith noticed that the Yoshinoya material had disappeared, even though it was the only bit of material they could remember. Considering how many great John Mulaney comedy specials we've gotten over the years, I can't help wondering how many other jokes disappeared during those early performances.

I'd love to know exactly what he was planning to say about Orange Julius, because that's another restaurant chain that feels tailor-made for a Mulaney routine. The Yoshinoya detail actually sent me down a bit of a rabbit hole because this isn't the first time the restaurant has figured into one of Mulaney's jokes.

Fans of Saturday Night Live might remember Bill Hader's hilarious return as Stefon in 2018 , during which Mulaney appeared as the character's attorney, Shy. At one point, he leaned over to whisper something into Hader's ear. Whatever he said caused Hader to completely lose his composure. Of course, Hader has a long history of losing it during Stefon appearances, and his inability to keep a straight face has produced some of SNL 's funniest unplanned moments.

Mark Tildesley , the acclaimed British production designer who worked on major titles including the last James Bond movie " No Time to Die ," has died. He was 63.

Tildesley is understood to have passed away on Nov. 24 following a long illness.

Across a career spanning more than 30 years, Tildesley collaborated with an array of leading directors both in the U.K. and beyond, on titles ranging from smaller indie film to big-budget Hollywood productions. Tildesley first joined forces with Boyle on his 2002 groundbreaking zombie hit "28 Days Later, but the two would team up again on films including "Millions," "Sunshine," "Trance" and "T2 Trainspotting." "Mark was a one-off: gentle, funny, warm, mischievous, entirely original and extraordinarily gifted," said Mendes. "My abiding memory of him is from 'Empire of Light,' flying down the Margate seafront on a motorised scooter, his technicolored scarf flapping in the wind, twinkling like a schoolboy playing hooky. A unique spirit and a wonderful artist. I am one of hundreds of people who are desperately sad that he is gone."

Other credits include Leigh's "Happy-Go-Lucky," Curtis' "The Boat that Rocked," Lone Scherfig's "One Day," Bill Condon's "The Fifth Estate," Wheatley's "High-Rise" and McDonagh's "The Banshees of Inisherin."
